previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of COPD, diastolic heart failure, obstructive sleep apnea, and morbid obesity was admitted for worsening shortness of breath. She presented with respiratory distress and elevated CO2, consistent with acute on chronic respiratory failure. Initial management included BiPAP, which was transitioned to nasal cannula due to noncompliance. Treatment focused on COPD exacerbation with steroids, nebulizers, and azithromycin, and acute on chronic heart failure with IV diuresis. A urine culture identified E. coli resistant to multiple antibiotics, and she was discharged on nitrofurantoin. Her symptoms improved, and she was discharged to extended care with a plan for medication adherence, CPAP compliance, and lab monitoring.

Acute Issues
============
# COPD, obesity hypoventilation sydrome, untreated sleep apnea: 
Patient reported poor adherence with her baseline oxygen 
requirement of ___, including ambulation without this which 
precipitated the desaturation that led to her admission.  
Pursed-lip breathing and accessory muscle use on admission 
raised concern for COPD exacerbation, Particularly given history 
of multiple tracheostomies and a recent MICU admission for BiPAP 
with prior exacerbations.  Of note, patient reports not 
receiving her nebulizers during the day at her nursing home.  
Started on standing nebulizers and a PO prednisone burst with 
return to baseline respiratory status on morning of HD1.  Of 
note, azithromycin not given due to prolonged QTc as below.
- Continue prednisone through ___ as below
- Please provide albuterol inhaler that patient may keep with 
her at all times, in addition to prn duonebs as prescribed below
.
# HFpEF: No obvious signs of volume overlaod on admission, with 
stable CXR and low BNP compared with prior admissions.  That 
said, patient reports worsening dietary indicretions starting ~ 
1 month ago ___ food), which correlated with the onset of 
her worsening respiratory status.  She also reports medication 
non-adherence, particularly with her increased lasix dose over 
the past week due to incontinence.  All of these are more likely 
contributory to chronic worsening dyspnea rather than the acute 
exacerbation.  Unfortunately she does not allow herself to be 
weighed frequently at her nursing home, so we do not know her 
dry weight.  Continued pre-admission oral lasix in-house, with 
good urine output, as well as metoprolol and lisinopril. Her 
kidney function remained normal.
- Weigh daily, titrate diuretics to lowest recent weight in 
facility records
.
# Prolonged QTc: 497 on admisson EKG, 506 on morning of HD1. EKG 
also showed sinu bradycardia. New relative to prior EKGs, most 
recently ___.  Did not give azithromycin for COPD 
exacerbation as above.  Also did not prescribe pre-admission 
trazadone, as this can prolong QTc.  We avoided all QT 
prolonging agents and this should be continued as an outpatient. 

-EKG daily for the next week, monitor QT,avoid all QT prolonging 
agents including pre-admission trazadone and fluoxetine. If it 
continues to be prolonged pt should be seen by a cardiologist as 
an outpatient.
.
